title.en: To Seek and Save the Lost

main_point.en: A real encounter with Jesus changes our hearts and our actions.
main_point.zh-Hant: 真正遇見耶穌會改變我們的心和行動。

christ_connection.en: Just as Jesus saw Zacchaeus, He sees each of us. He calls us out of our sin and into a life of faithful obedience.
christ_connection.zh-Hant: 正如耶穌看見撒該，祂也看見我們每一個人。祂呼召我們離開罪，進入忠心順服的生活。

title.en: Jesus Meets Us Where We Are
title.zh-Hant: 耶穌在我們所在之處與我們相遇

content.en:
1 He entered Jericho and was passing through.
2 And behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector and was rich.
3 And he was seeking to see who Jesus was, but on account of the crowd he could not, because he was small in stature.
4 So he ran on ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was about to pass that way.
5 And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for I must stay at your house today.”
content.zh-Hant:
1 耶穌進了耶利哥，正經過的時候，
2 有一個人名叫撒該，作稅吏長，是個財主。
3 他要看看耶穌是怎樣的人；只因人多，他的身量又矮，所以不得看見，
4 就跑到前頭，爬上桑樹，要看耶穌，因為耶穌必從那裏經過。
5 耶穌到了那裏，抬頭一看，對他說：「撒該，快下來！今天我必住在你家裏。」

content.en:
6 So he hurried and came down and received him joyfully.
7 And when they saw it, they all grumbled, “He has gone in to be the guest of a man who is a sinner.”
8 And Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor. And if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore it fourfold.”
9 And Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, since he also is a son of Abraham.
10 For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”
content.zh-Hant:
6 他就急忙下來，歡歡喜喜地接待耶穌。
7 眾人看見，都私下議論說：「他竟到罪人家裏去住宿。」
8 撒該站著對主說：「主啊，我把所有的一半給窮人；我若訛詐了誰，就還他四倍。」
9 耶穌說：「今天救恩到了這家，因為他也是亞伯拉罕的子孫。
10 人子來，為要尋找、拯救失喪的人。」

content.en: Leaders: You may have many students who identify with Zacchaeus on a deeply painful level; they struggle with being the outcast or with being labeled unworthy. What a beautiful moment to show them how much Jesus cares for them—how He invites them.
content.zh-Hant: 領袖：你可能有許多學生深切體會撒該的痛苦；他們因被排斥或被貼上不配的標籤而掙扎。這是多麼美好的時刻，可以讓他們看見耶穌多麼關心他們，以及祂如何邀請他們。

title.en: Jesus Meets Us Where We Are
title.zh-Hant: 耶穌在我們所在之處與我們相遇

content.en: “Regular tax collectors were hated in Israel because they worked for the Roman government that oppressed the Jewish people. Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector. In all likelihood he did not receive that position by working hard. He probably rose to that rank by being more crooked than other tax collectors, who often cheated people out of their earnings.”⁸
content.zh-Hant: 「一般的稅吏在以色列受人憎恨，因為他們為壓迫猶太人的羅馬政府工作。撒該是稅吏長。他很可能不是憑勤奮工作得到這個職位，而是比其他常常騙取人們收入的稅吏更加不正直，才升到這個地位。」⁸

content.en: “Zacchaeus provides us a marvelous picture of repentance. He also provides us a marvelous picture of Luke 18:27. Here God demonstrates the ‘possible’ salvation in a rich man’s life. God can call people from all their idols, a lifetime of sin, and the habit of abusing privilege, position, and others, and turn such persons to Himself, making them new.”⁹
content.zh-Hant: 「撒該為我們呈現了一幅美妙的悔改圖畫，也為我們呈現了路加福音 18:27 的美妙圖畫。神在這裏顯明，一個富人得救是『可能』的。神能呼召人離開他們所有的偶像、一生的罪，以及濫用特權、地位和欺壓他人的習慣，使這些人歸向祂，成為新造的人。」⁹

content.en: “Despite the protests of Pharisees (5:30; 7:39; 15:2-3) or Pharisaic types (19:7), salvation came to the outcasts, who responded in repentance and faith (or who by their actions [19:8] revealed their repentance and faith). Luke never tired of this theme of the great reversal. With each example he sought to reassure his readers that salvation had come to them even though they were outcasts, i.e., Gentiles. The Son of Man did not come for the righteous but for lost people, like them. It is for sinners that Jesus has come, and there is no other way of salvation than the way of Zacchaeus, the prodigal son, and other sinners. Apart from the prayer of the tax collector (‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner,’ 18:13), there can be no salvation. If this offends the self-righteous, so be it. There is no other gospel, for ‘the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost’ (19:10).”¹⁰
content.zh-Hant: 「儘管法利賽人（5:30；7:39；15:2-3）或像法利賽人的人（19:7）提出抗議，救恩仍臨到被排斥的人；他們以悔改和信心回應，或藉著行動（19:8）顯明他們的悔改與信心。路加從不厭倦這個大逆轉的主題。他藉著每一個例子，努力讓讀者確信，雖然他們是被排斥的人，也就是外邦人，救恩仍已臨到他們。人子來不是為了義人，而是為了像他們這樣失喪的人。耶穌是為罪人而來；除了撒該、浪子和其他罪人所走的路，再沒有別的得救之道。若沒有稅吏的禱告（『神啊，開恩可憐我這個罪人！』18:13），就不可能得救。如果這冒犯了自義的人，那就由他們去吧。沒有別的福音，因為『人子來，為要尋找、拯救失喪的人』（19:10）。」¹⁰

content.en: This passage, though familiar, is one of the clearest reflections of God’s heart for the lost—for all people. Jesus made a radical move when He interacted with a man labeled by fellow Jews as an unworthy traitor. Zacchaeus was a Jewish tax collector—a chief tax collector (v. 2). This position set him apart from most Jews because it meant working for the enemy, for Rome. In exchange for a more lavish lifestyle and financial benefits, Zacchaeus collected taxes from the Jews, inflating them further for his own profit. In essence, Zacchaeus stole from his own people, adding oppression on top of oppression. Because Zacchaeus was one of them, the betrayal cut more deeply. Of all people to seek out Jesus, Zacchaeus was the one who ran and climbed a tree, breaking all the social norms of the day. Both Jesus and Zacchaeus faced opposition from the watching crowd, and their conversation had serious implications for both of them. The moment Zacchaeus’s path intersected with Jesus’s path, he faced a decision: Would he surrender or would he walk “away sorrowful, for he had great possessions” (Matt. 19:22), like the rich young ruler who gripped tightly to earthly possessions, missing heavenly treasure?
content.zh-Hant: 這段經文雖然為人熟悉，卻是最清楚反映神對失喪之人，對所有人的心意的經文之一。耶穌與一個被同胞猶太人視為不配的叛徒交往，做了一件突破常規的事。撒該是猶太稅吏，而且是稅吏長（第 2 節）。這職位使他與大多數猶太人不同，因為這意味著他為敵人羅馬工作。為換取更奢華的生活和經濟利益，撒該向猶太人收稅，額外加徵以中飽私囊。撒該實際上是偷取自己同胞的錢，在壓迫之上加添壓迫。因為撒該是他們的同胞，這背叛更加傷人。在所有尋求耶穌的人當中，撒該竟跑起來並爬上樹，打破當時所有的社會規範。耶穌和撒該都面對旁觀群眾的反對，他們的對話對雙方都有重大意義。撒該與耶穌相遇的那一刻，他面臨一個決定：他會降服，還是像那緊抓地上財產而錯過天上財寶的年輕官員一樣，「憂憂愁愁地走了，因為他的產業很多」（馬太福音 19:22）？

content.en: Guilt refers to the objective status of someone being found guilty for a wrong committed, as well as the incurring of punishment that comes with it (Matt. 5:21-22; James 2:10). Shame is the emotional pain that comes from sinful actions. Scripture teaches that humans are guilty before God and often experience deep feelings of shame.
content.zh-Hant: 罪責指一個人因所犯的錯被判有罪的客觀狀態，以及隨之而來的刑罰（馬太福音 5:21-22；雅各書 2:10）。羞恥是犯罪行為帶來的情緒痛苦。聖經教導，人類在神面前有罪，也常常經歷深深的羞恥感。

content.en: God, help us to seek Jesus. Help us to see You clearly and move us to action so that we can point others to You. Let our lives be completely changed by the truth of who You are and by the fact that You invite us, sinners, to follow You.
content.zh-Hant: 神啊，求祢幫助我們尋求耶穌，幫助我們清楚看見祢，並感動我們採取行動，好把別人引向祢。願我們的生命因祢身分的真理，以及祢邀請我們這些罪人跟隨祢的事實而完全改變。

question.en: What’s more important—a lot of money or a lot of friends (1=Rich but lonely; 10=Friends but broke)?
question.zh-Hant: 甚麼更重要：許多金錢還是許多朋友？（1＝富有卻孤單；10＝有朋友卻身無分文）

instructions.en:
These optional activities are designed to help your students interact. You’ll find a Discussion Activity and a Cultural Connection, which touches on a relevant topic in today’s teen culture. Each group is different, so adapt these activities to fit your group’s needs. The goal is for students to connect more to the lesson as they connect to the topic and to one another.

Ask the following questions, allowing time for students to share responses:
instructions.zh-Hant:
這些可自由選用的活動旨在幫助學生互動。你會找到一個討論活動和一個文化連結，後者涉及當今青少年文化中的相關話題。每個小組都不同，請調整這些活動以符合你小組的需要。目的是讓學生在彼此連結、接觸主題的同時，更投入本課。

提出以下問題，並留時間讓學生分享答案：

question.en: When has your height either helped you or kept you from doing something?
question.zh-Hant: 你的身高曾在甚麼時候幫助你或阻礙你做某件事？

question.en: If your favorite celebrity, singer, or athlete was going to be in town, what length would you go to meet him or her?
question.zh-Hant: 如果你最喜愛的名人、歌手或運動員來到你的城市，你會為見他或她付出多大努力？

question.en: What are some crazy lengths people have gone to so they could be near someone they looked up to?
question.zh-Hant: 人們曾為了接近自己仰慕的人，做出哪些瘋狂的事？

content.en: Some of us would go to drastic lengths to get close to people we admire, even if others think we’re crazy. But imagine this person looking you in the eye and calling you by name! Today, we'll see that Jesus did so much more for Zacchaeus than he ever could have imagined. He called him by name and wanted to spend time with him, despite his life choices and career.
content.zh-Hant: 我們有些人會不惜一切接近自己仰慕的人，即使別人認為我們瘋了。但想像一下，這個人看著你的眼睛，叫出你的名字！今天我們會看見，耶穌為撒該所做的遠超過他所能想像。儘管撒該選擇了那樣的生活和職業，耶穌仍叫出他的名字，並想與他共度時間。

cultural_connection.en: First impressions really do matter. Think of someone you didn’t have a great first impression of: Has that carried over into how you view that person now? Once we put labels on people, removing them is difficult, even if we misunderstood their character. The label leaves a sticky residue that takes a lot of time and effort to remove. If someone we’ve labeled has something amazing happen, we may struggle to feel he or she deserves it. We tend to have a hard time forgetting first impressions, even when we’re wrong and the labels are unfair. See if you can turn this situation around and put yourself in their shoes. Would you hope others would remove an inaccurate label much sooner if circumstances had changed in your life? If you changed? Sure. So, when we realize that our first impression of someone was wrong, or when we realize the person has changed, let’s remove those labels and choose to see others the way God sees them. Let’s take it one step further and resist placing labels at all.
cultural_connection.zh-Hant: 第一印象確實重要。想想一個你對他第一印象不太好的人：這是否影響了你現在對他的看法？我們一旦給人貼上標籤，就很難撕掉，即使我們誤解了他的品格也是如此。標籤會留下黏膠般的痕跡，需要花許多時間和努力才能清除。當被我們貼標籤的人遇到美好的事，我們可能很難覺得他配得。即使我們錯了，標籤並不公平，我們往往仍難以忘記第一印象。試著把情況反過來，設身處地為他們著想。如果你的生活環境改變了，或你改變了，你會希望別人早點撕掉不準確的標籤嗎？當然會。因此，當我們意識到自己對某人的第一印象錯了，或發現這個人已經改變，就讓我們撕掉那些標籤，選擇像神一樣看待別人。讓我們更進一步，避免給人貼標籤。

title.en: Jesus Meets Us Where We Are
title.zh-Hant: 耶穌在我們所在之處與我們相遇

question.en: Why do you think Luke included Zacchaeus’s job and social status?
question.zh-Hant: 你認為路加為甚麼記載撒該的職業和社會地位？

answer.en: Leaders: Share Context about tax collectors. Jesus ministered to all kinds of people, but the Gospel writers didn’t always mention their backgrounds. Luke noted that Zacchaeus was a rich tax collector. These men were despised by fellow Jews, viewed as traitors and lumped together with “sinners.” Luke communicated that Jesus calls everyone. Zacchaeus—and the people watching— needed to know that following Jesus came at a cost. Zacchaeus couldn’t keep functioning as he did before, especially since most of his wealth was stolen from others. His stained reputation would take time to change, but encountering Jesus changed his heart quickly.
answer.zh-Hant: 領袖：分享背景中關於稅吏的內容。耶穌服事各式各樣的人，但福音書作者並不總是提及他們的背景。路加指出撒該是一個富有的稅吏。這些人被同胞猶太人藐視，視為叛徒，與「罪人」歸為一類。路加傳達的是耶穌呼召所有人。撒該和旁觀的人需要知道，跟隨耶穌是要付代價的。撒該不能繼續像以前一樣行事，尤其因為他大部分財富都是從別人那裏偷來的。他受損的名聲需要時間才能改變，但遇見耶穌很快就改變了他的心。

question.en: What keeps us from making an effort to get to Jesus—to see Him and know Him?
question.zh-Hant: 甚麼阻礙我們努力來到耶穌面前，看見並認識祂？

answer.en: Zacchaeus’s height kept him from seeing Jesus, so he took drastic steps to get a better view. Men of his social status wouldn’t run or climb trees for any reason, but societal rules didn’t stop Zacchaeus. Jesus had changed people’s lives; if everything Zacchaeus heard was true and Jesus was who he thought He was, then maybe Zacchaeus had hope for himself. We often care too much about what others think to make this kind of effort to be closer to Jesus. We let shame tell us that Jesus won’t respond to us because we don’t deserve His attention. But Jesus sees us and invites us closer.
answer.zh-Hant: 撒該的身高使他看不見耶穌，於是他採取了不尋常的行動，好看得更清楚。像他這樣有社會地位的男人，無論如何都不會跑步或爬樹，但社會規範沒有攔阻撒該。耶穌曾改變人的生命；如果撒該所聽見的一切都是真的，而耶穌正是他所想的那位，也許撒該自己就有盼望。我們往往太在乎別人的看法，以致不願這樣努力親近耶穌。我們容許羞恥告訴自己，耶穌不會回應我們，因為我們不配得到祂的關注。但耶穌看見我們，邀請我們親近祂。

question.en: What’s the significance of Jesus calling Zacchaeus by name?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌叫出撒該的名字有甚麼意義？

answer.en: Jesus knew Zacchaeus, even though they had never met. Jesus knows you by name. He knows your story (even the parts you don’t want Him to know) and still seeks you out for relationship with Him. Maybe you’ve always had this idea that Jesus was standoffish or disappointed in you— that if He was standing in front of you, He might look past you at people who better fit a religious mold. But the Gospels show us that Jesus isn’t like this at all. We see Jesus step into people’s stories right where He’s needed—in their mess, in their pain, before they’ve had a chance to clean up their lives. The people watching must have wondered how, of all people, Jesus knew Zacchaeus—a tax collector who made his wealth off of working for Rome, the great enemy. They must’ve wondered why Jesus wanted to stay at his house, but Jesus wasn’t worried about their opinions. He had business with Zacchaeus and called him out by name. He does the same for us. No matter our backgrounds, the sins we’ve committed, the messy family situations we’re in, Jesus sees us, knows us, and calls us by name.
answer.zh-Hant: 耶穌認識撒該，儘管他們從未見過面。耶穌知道你的名字。祂知道你的故事，甚至包括你不想讓祂知道的部分，卻仍然尋找你，要與你建立關係。也許你一直認為耶穌冷漠疏遠，或對你感到失望；如果祂站在你面前，祂可能會越過你，去看那些更符合宗教標準的人。但福音書讓我們看見，耶穌完全不是這樣。我們看見耶穌走進人們的故事，就在他們需要祂的地方——在他們的混亂和痛苦中，在他們有機會整理好自己的生活之前。旁觀的人一定想知道，這麼多人當中，耶穌怎會認識撒該，一個為強大的敵人羅馬工作而致富的稅吏。他們一定想知道耶穌為甚麼要住在他家，但耶穌不在乎他們的意見。祂有事要在撒該身上成就，並叫出他的名字。祂也這樣對待我們。不論我們的背景、所犯的罪，或身處多麼混亂的家庭處境，耶穌都看見我們、認識我們，並按名呼召我們。

question.en: How did the people in the crowd view Zacchaeus?
question.zh-Hant: 群眾如何看待撒該？

answer.en: The crowd labeled Zacchaeus a sinful man. Zacchaeus was a tax collector and a thief. In their eyes, he could produce nothing good. The idea that Jesus wanted to spend time with him was insane in the eyes of those watching. Zacchaeus wasn’t the kind of person they expected Jesus to surround Himself with. The crowd complained about Zacchaeus, even though they couldn’t possibly know his whole story; they couldn’t possibly know Zacchaeus’s heart, his insecurities, his doubts and fears. Zacchaeus’s heart was open and ready for change—he intentionally looked for Jesus and did everything he could to get near Him. He was willing to let Jesus change everything about him.
answer.zh-Hant: 群眾給撒該貼上罪人的標籤。撒該是稅吏，也是賊。在他們眼中，他做不出任何好事。對旁觀的人來說，耶穌想與他共度時間的想法簡直瘋狂。撒該不是他們預期耶穌會親近的人。群眾抱怨撒該，雖然他們不可能知道他的全部故事，也不可能知道他的心、不安、疑惑和恐懼。撒該敞開心，準備好改變；他刻意尋找耶穌，並盡一切所能接近祂。他願意讓耶穌改變他的一切。

question.en: Why was Zacchaeus willing to give away his money so freely? How is he an example for us?
question.zh-Hant: 撒該為甚麼願意如此慷慨地把錢分出去？他如何成為我們的榜樣？

answer.en: For Zacchaeus, knowing and following Jesus was worth losing wealth. Zacchaeus realized that Jesus was willing to see him as someone other than a “tax collector,” so his earthly possessions lost their significance. The burden of his theft weighed heavily on him, and he wanted to make things right with people he had wronged. A relationship with Jesus mattered more than his pride and his riches. Zacchaeus could no longer keep doing what he had always done and was willing to make a change. If we’re honest, the weight of our sin is heavy. Carrying the weight of people’s expectations, the weight of their judgment, or the weight of feeling like we can’t change is exhausting. Jesus really does invite us to lay it all down to follow Him. As He did with Zacchaeus, Jesus really can transform us and free us from who we’ve always been.
answer.zh-Hant: 對撒該來說，認識並跟隨耶穌值得他失去財富。撒該意識到，耶穌願意看見他不只是個「稅吏」，因此他地上的財產失去了原有的重要性。他偷竊的重擔沉重地壓在他心上，他想彌補自己虧欠的人。與耶穌的關係比他的驕傲和財富更重要。撒該不能再繼續照舊行事，他願意改變。坦白說，我們的罪是沉重的。背負別人的期望、他們的評斷，或覺得自己無法改變的重擔，令人筋疲力盡。耶穌確實邀請我們放下一切來跟隨祂。正如祂對撒該所做的，耶穌真的能改變我們，使我們從一向的舊我中得自由。

question.en: What difference has meeting Jesus made for you?
question.zh-Hant: 遇見耶穌為你帶來了甚麼改變？

answer.en: Meeting Jesus changed Zacchaeus. His heart searched for Jesus, and Jesus set everything else aside to speak with a man no one else wanted anything to do with. Jesus was on mission to “seek and save the lost,” and Zacchaeus was ready to be found, no matter the cost. Here’s the truth: We see no evidence in Scripture that we can follow Jesus and remain the same. In every case, those who follow Jesus are changed by Him. Those who choose not to follow Him remain the same. Knowing Jesus must make a difference in our hearts, and that difference flows into every area of our lives as evidence for others to see.
answer.zh-Hant: 遇見耶穌改變了撒該。他的心尋求耶穌，而耶穌放下其他一切，與一個沒有人願意交往的人說話。耶穌的使命是「尋找、拯救失喪的人」，撒該則準備好被尋見，不論代價如何。事實是：我們在聖經中看不見任何證據表明，我們可以跟隨耶穌卻保持原樣。每一個跟隨耶穌的人都被祂改變；選擇不跟隨祂的人則保持原樣。認識耶穌必定會改變我們的心，這改變會流露到生活的每個層面，成為別人能看見的證據。

question.en: When have you felt stuck because you didn’t want to let Jesus change a part of your life? What would surrendering it look like?
question.zh-Hant: 你曾在甚麼時候因不願讓耶穌改變你生命中的某一部分而感到停滯不前？將它交託給祂會是甚麼樣子？

answer.en: The beautiful truth about the Lord is that He doesn’t desire forced obedience. He desires our willing surrender. Many of us struggle to surrender certain parts of ourselves. We cling to certain pieces of our lives because we don’t want those pieces to change. We're scared of what that change might bring. But knowing and following Jesus is worth changing everything in our lives. He is worth obeying because anything He calls us away from is a lesser love. Sacrificing what is valuable in the world pales in comparison to the sacrifice Jesus made for us. Dietrich Bonhoeffer, a theologian who was imprisoned and killed for resisting the Nazi regime in WWII, explained it this way: “What has cost God much cannot be cheap for us.”¹¹ Following Jesus is costly, but it is worth the cost. Zacchaeus saw this with his own eyes and knew he needed Jesus more than anything money could buy. We may not see the full reward of following Jesus on this side of heaven, but we will in eternity. And we will never regret giving Him everything we have.
answer.zh-Hant: 關於主的美好真理是，祂不渴望強迫的順服，而是渴望我們甘心降服。我們許多人很難交出自己的某些部分。我們緊抓著生活中的某些事物，因為我們不想它們改變，也害怕改變可能帶來的後果。但認識並跟隨耶穌值得我們改變生命中的一切。祂值得我們順服，因為祂呼召我們離開的任何事物，都比不上愛祂。與耶穌為我們所作的犧牲相比，犧牲世人看為寶貴的東西就顯得微不足道。神學家潘霍華因在第二次世界大戰期間抵抗納粹政權而被囚禁和殺害，他這樣解釋：「使神付出重價的，對我們來說不可能是廉價的。」¹¹ 跟隨耶穌要付代價，但這代價是值得的。撒該親眼看見這一點，知道自己需要耶穌，勝過金錢所能買到的一切。我們可能在今生看不見跟隨耶穌的全部賞賜，但在永恆中會看見。我們永遠不會後悔把自己所有的一切交給祂。

content.en:
Most of us have probably completed seek and find puzzles. You have to meticulously look for items within a larger picture, and these items may be hidden within other items or drawn in a way that disguises them as something else.

In our main lesson this week and in today’s passage, we see that seeking and finding is what Jesus came to earth to do, but He seeks and finds us for salvation and a relationship with Him. When Jesus told Zacchaeus that He was going to stay at his house, the crowd following Jesus was displeased because Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector. Tax collectors were Jewish men who collected taxes for Rome but also took above what was required to fill their own pockets. As a chief tax collector, Zacchaeus was the worst of the worst—a betrayer of his people and a crook. But Jesus explained to the crowd that He came “to seek and save the lost” (Luke 19:10).

Jesus was quoting directly from today’s passage. He answered the crowd’s complaints with Scripture about the Messiah—about Himself. Those who made the connection would recognize that the Shepherd Messiah came to seek out the stray sheep—those who had lost their way—to heal and strengthen them. Zacchaeus was exactly that. Like a lost sheep, he had lost his way— extorted his fellow Jews, worked for the oppressing government, and lived for himself. But he repented and believed, and Jesus welcomed Zacchaeus into His flock.

Jesus, our Good Shepherd, sought Zacchaeus out, bringing salvation to him. Jesus does the same for us. He seeks us out and offers us salvation, but He doesn’t just save us. He brings us into His flock, heals our wounds, and strengthens us.
content.zh-Hant:
我們大多數人可能都玩過尋物遊戲。你必須在一幅較大的圖畫中仔細尋找物件，而這些物件可能藏在其他物件之中，或被畫成其他東西的樣子。

在本週的主要課文和今天的經文中，我們看見尋找和尋見是耶穌來到地上的目的；祂尋找並尋見我們，是為了拯救我們，並與我們建立關係。當耶穌告訴撒該祂要住在他家時，跟隨耶穌的群眾很不高興，因為撒該是稅吏長。稅吏是為羅馬收稅的猶太人，他們收取超過規定的款項，中飽私囊。身為稅吏長，撒該是最壞的人，是背叛同胞的騙子。但耶穌向群眾解釋，祂來是「為要尋找、拯救失喪的人」（路加福音 19:10）。

耶穌直接引用了今天的經文。祂用關於彌賽亞、也就是關於祂自己的經文回答群眾的抱怨。能聯想到的人會認出，牧人彌賽亞來是要尋找迷途的羊，就是那些迷失方向的人，醫治並堅固他們。撒該正是這樣的人。他像迷途的羊一樣迷失了方向：勒索猶太同胞、為壓迫人的政府工作，又為自己而活。但他悔改相信，耶穌便歡迎撒該進入祂的羊群。

耶穌，我們的好牧人，尋找撒該，為他帶來救恩。耶穌也這樣對待我們。祂尋找我們，向我們提供救恩，卻不只是拯救我們；祂把我們帶進祂的羊群，醫治我們的傷口，堅固我們。

question.en: What does this passage about the Shepherd Messiah tell you about Jesus’s character?
question.zh-Hant: 這段關於牧人彌賽亞的經文讓你認識耶穌有甚麼品格？

question.en: How does knowing that Jesus sought you out, like Zacchaeus, deepen your love for Him?
question.zh-Hant: 知道耶穌像尋找撒該一樣尋找你，如何加深你對祂的愛？

prayer.en: Jesus, You are the Good Shepherd. You sought me and found me. You brought me into Your flock, and I am so grateful.
prayer.zh-Hant: 耶穌，祢是好牧人。祢尋找我，也找到了我。祢把我帶進祢的羊群，我非常感恩。

content.en:
Zacchaeus’s encounter with Jesus was life-changing. He was a new man, giving away his riches and attempting to generously right those he wronged. Encountering Jesus changes us in ways we would never even imagine. Paul explained in today’s passage that before salvation, we were dead. But God loves us so much that, through Christ, He makes us alive!

So what does that mean? Without Jesus, we walk like the world. But in Christ, we walk according to His ways. For example, before knowing Jesus, maybe you didn’t see the problem with a little gossip, but after Christ, you work to build others up (Eph. 4:29). Before Christ, obeying your parents wasn’t cool, but after Christ, you really work to honor them (Col. 3:20). Before Christ, you used foul language, but after Christ, you choose words that honor the Lord (Col. 3:8). Before Christ, you may have cheated on your homework, project, or test, but after Christ, you do your work with integrity (Eph. 4:28).

Living in our new identities as Christ-followers can be difficult sometimes. Our lives are conformed to a different worldview. The Holy Spirit works in us, teaching, correcting, and growing us to be more like Christ every day. We must constantly say “no” to our flesh, which we used to say “yes” to. Growth can be painful, but God loves us too much to leave us in the state we were in. He doesn’t just want us to live barely alive, but He wants us to thrive and to make an eternal impact. The good news? We don’t do this alone. We do it with the power of Christ who lives in us (Phil. 4:13).
content.zh-Hant:
撒該與耶穌相遇，生命從此改變。他成了一個新的人，分給別人財富，並嘗試慷慨地彌補自己虧欠的人。遇見耶穌會以我們從未想像過的方式改變我們。保羅在今天的經文中解釋，得救之前我們是死的。但神如此愛我們，祂藉著基督使我們活過來！

這是甚麼意思？沒有耶穌，我們就像世人一樣行事；但在基督裏，我們按照祂的道路而行。例如，認識耶穌之前，也許你覺得說點閒話沒有問題；但在基督裏，你努力造就別人（以弗所書 4:29）。認識基督之前，你覺得順服父母不酷；但在基督裏，你努力尊敬他們（歌羅西書 3:20）。認識基督之前，你說污穢的話；但在基督裏，你選擇榮耀主的言語（歌羅西書 3:8）。認識基督之前，你可能在功課、專題或考試中作弊；但在基督裏，你誠實地完成自己的工作（以弗所書 4:28）。

以基督跟隨者的新身分生活有時並不容易。我們的生活要按照不同的世界觀而改變。聖靈在我們裏面工作，教導、糾正我們，幫助我們成長，使我們每天更像基督。我們必須不斷對從前順從的肉體說「不」。成長可能痛苦，但神太愛我們，不會讓我們停留在原來的狀態。祂不只希望我們勉強活著，更希望我們蓬勃成長，產生永恆的影響。好消息是甚麼？我們不是獨自做到這些，而是靠著住在我們裏面的基督的能力（腓立比書 4:13）。

question.en: How has knowing Jesus changed you? How does He continue to make you new? What do you need to give to the Lord to work on?
question.zh-Hant: 認識耶穌如何改變了你？祂如何繼續更新你？你需要把甚麼交給主，讓祂在其中工作？

question.en: Why is it sometimes difficult to follow Jesus? How do you know a relationship with Him is worth it?
question.zh-Hant: 跟隨耶穌有時為甚麼困難？你如何知道與祂建立關係是值得的？

prayer.en: Jesus, You are worth all the growing pains because You have brought me from death to life. Grow me to be more and more like You every day.
prayer.zh-Hant: 耶穌，因為祢帶我出死入生，所有成長的痛苦都值得。求祢使我每天成長，越來越像祢。

content.en:
Zacchaeus promised to give half his possessions to the poor and pay back those he stole from, but this wasn’t how he was saved; He did this because Jesus saved him. He believed Jesus was who He said He was—the Messiah. And because of this, the greed and selfishness that once defined Zacchaeus’s reputation and life were immediately changed and he couldn't help but give his possessions away.

Paul, in today’s passage, said that we are saved by faith, not works. Salvation is a gift from God; we can never do anything to deserve it. But, when we join the family of God, Jesus works in us, changing us to be more and more like Him. And the evidence of His work in us is good works. He continually molds and fashions us for His kingdom work.

You might be thinking, “I’m just a teenager. How in the world can the Lord use me for His good works?” The Bible is full of young people who God used for His glory—Joseph, David, Esther, Daniel, Mary, Jeremiah. He didn’t save you just to say, “Okay, hang tight until you’re an adult. Maybe I can use you then.” God has prepared ahead of time and the Holy Spirit is working in you now for His good works. You weren't just saved from something but for something!
content.zh-Hant:
撒該應許把一半財產分給窮人，並償還那些被他偷取財物的人，但這不是他得救的方式；他這樣做是因為耶穌拯救了他。他相信耶穌就是祂所說的那位——彌賽亞。因此，曾經定義撒該名聲和生活的貪婪與自私立刻改變了，他忍不住把財產分給別人。

在今天的經文中，保羅說我們因信得救，而非靠行為。救恩是神的禮物；我們永遠不能做任何事使自己配得救恩。但當我們加入神的家，耶穌便在我們裏面工作，改變我們，使我們越來越像祂。祂在我們裏面工作的證據就是善行。祂不斷塑造我們，讓我們參與祂國度的工作。

你可能在想：「我只是個青少年，主究竟怎能用我去行祂的善工？」聖經中有許多年輕人被神使用，為祂帶來榮耀：例如約瑟、大衛、以斯帖、但以理、馬利亞、耶利米。祂拯救你，並不是只為了說：「好，等你長大成人吧，也許到時我可以使用你。」神已預先作好準備，聖靈現在就在你裏面工作，使你行祂的善工。你得救不只是脫離某些事，也是為了某個目的！

question.en: Think through the young people named in the Bible. How did God use them for His good works?
question.zh-Hant: 想想聖經中提到的年輕人。神如何使用他們行祂的善工？

question.en: How can God use you now for His good works? Where is the Holy Spirit prompting you to join God’s kingdom work this week?
question.zh-Hant: 神現在如何使用你行祂的善工？本週聖靈正感動你在哪方面參與神國度的工作？

prayer.en: Lord, You created me for a purpose. Use me for Your good works. When I don’t feel ready for the task, remind me that You are the One doing the work through me!
prayer.zh-Hant: 主啊，祢創造我是有目的的。求祢使用我行祢的善工。當我覺得自己還未準備好接受任務時，求祢提醒我，是祢透過我在工作！

content.en:
Just as we saw in this week’s main lesson, Zacchaeus’s faith in Jesus transformed his mind and heart, and as a result, his actions. Likewise, our actions should reflect the transformation Jesus has done in us. Paul urged the Colossian church, and us, to “walk worthy of the Lord” (v. 10). And he tells us what that looks like in the following verses: bear fruit in good works, grow in the knowledge of God, be strengthened in endurance and patience, and give thanks to the Lord. This isn’t a complete list, but Paul was encouraging Christ-followers to live their lives in a manner that shows we are citizens of Jesus’s kingdom.

What does it practically mean to “walk in a manner worthy of the Lord”? Our actions should match our words. When we “walk worthy,” we choose to live our lives in a way that brings honor and glory to God and points others to Jesus. We’re kind, loving, joyful, patient, and gentle with others (Gal. 5:22-23). We study God’s Word so that we can know Him better. The Bible is God’s revelation of Himself and His work in this world. We must know it to know Him. When difficult times comes, we persevere and lean into Jesus. He will help us endure and develop patience. And we live a life full of gratitude as children of God. Because of our inheritance in the family of God, we aren't just saved from hell but we are coheirs of God’s kingdom (Rom. 8:16-17)!

We were dead, headed to hell, entrapped in darkness, and hopeless, but God, in His great love for us, sent His perfect Son to exchange our punishment for His redemption. Our sins are forgiven and we are now part of the kingdom of Jesus. God’s love is the only reason this happened, and in our overwhelming gratitude for our great rescue, we choose to walk in His ways. We choose to live a life worthy of His sacrifice. We choose to live a life that pleases Him.
content.zh-Hant:
正如我們在本週主要課文中所見，撒該對耶穌的信改變了他的心思和內心，因而也改變了他的行動。同樣，我們的行動應當反映耶穌在我們裏面所成就的改變。保羅勸勉歌羅西教會，也勸勉我們，要「行事為人對得起主」（第 10 節）。他在接下來的經文中告訴我們這是甚麼樣子：在善事上結果子、漸漸多認識神、得著力量忍耐寬容，並感謝主。這並非完整的清單，但保羅是在鼓勵基督的跟隨者以生活表明自己是耶穌國度的子民。

在實際生活中，「行事為人對得起主」是甚麼意思？我們的行動應當與言語一致。當我們「行事為人對得起主」，我們就選擇以尊崇榮耀神、引領別人歸向耶穌的方式生活。我們以仁慈、愛心、喜樂、忍耐和溫柔對待別人（加拉太書 5:22-23）。我們研讀神的話，好更認識祂。聖經是神對自己及祂在世界上工作的啟示；我們必須認識聖經，才能認識祂。當困難來臨，我們堅持並倚靠耶穌；祂會幫助我們忍耐，培養耐心。我們也作為神的兒女，過充滿感恩的生活。因為我們在神家中所得的基業，我們不只是從地獄得救，還是神國的共同後嗣（羅馬書 8:16-17）！

我們曾是死的，走向地獄，被黑暗困住，毫無盼望；但神因對我們的大愛，差遣祂完美的兒子承受我們的刑罰，換來祂的救贖。我們的罪得赦免，如今成為耶穌國度的一部分。這一切發生的唯一原因是神的愛；我們因蒙受偉大拯救而滿懷感恩，選擇行在祂的道路上，選擇活出與祂的犧牲相稱的生命，選擇過討祂喜悅的生活。

question.en: What does walking worthy look like in your life?
question.zh-Hant: 在你的生活中，行事為人對得起主是甚麼樣子？

question.en: What daily habits need to change so that you are living a life that pleases the Lord?
question.zh-Hant: 哪些日常習慣需要改變，才能使你的生活蒙主喜悅？

prayer.en: Lord, help me to live my life with gratitude for all You have done. Help me walk worthy so that I may please You.
prayer.zh-Hant: 主啊，求祢幫助我為祢所做的一切存感恩的心生活，幫助我行事為人對得起祢，使我能討祢喜悅。

content.en:
Zacchaeus climbed a tree to “see who Jesus was” (Luke 19:3), and later in the passage, Jesus told everyone exactly who He is—the Son of Man. Today’s passage includes what many call a “Christ Hymn,” which is simply a passage that magnifies Jesus and His work.

How would you answer the question, “Who is Jesus?” Paul wrote that He is the Lord and Redeemer of creation. He is the visible expression of God. He is the Creator—all things were made through Him. While God might be viewed as the architect of creation, Jesus is the foreman. Creation came about through His power and ability. All things were also made for Him, which means creation exists to display His glory. Jesus is the Redeemer of creation. Everything that was once warped by sin will now be touched by His grace—and He is the head of it. Creation had to be reconciled, or pay the penalty for sin, but Jesus paid the penalty instead. And because He did, we are reconciled back to God, back to the relationship that the Lord created us for way back in the garden of Eden.

What Jesus has done for creation through His death on the cross is the only way we could ever have true peace and true fellowship with God. We are now holy, faultless, and blameless before Him! This is the good news of the gospel! Paul dedicated his life to sharing the gospel because of its greatness, and we are called to do the same. We have the benefit of the New Testament writers and their explanations of who Jesus is, but Zacchaeus wanted to see who He was for himself. And with the eyes of his heart, he recognized Jesus as his Lord and Redeemer and chose to trust in Him. For those of us who have done the same, we must dedicate ourselves in service of the gospel, declaring Jesus’s greatness throughout His creation.
content.zh-Hant:
撒該爬上一棵樹，要「看看耶穌是怎樣的人」（路加福音 19:3）；在這段經文後來的記載中，耶穌清楚告訴眾人祂是誰——人子。今天的經文包括許多人稱為「基督頌」的段落，就是一段頌揚耶穌和祂作為的經文。

你會如何回答「耶穌是誰」這個問題？保羅寫道，祂是受造界的主和救贖主，是神看得見的彰顯。祂是創造主，萬有都藉著祂而造。如果把神看作創造的建築師，耶穌就是工程的領班；創造是藉著祂的能力成就的。萬有也都是為祂而造，這意味著受造界的存在是為了彰顯祂的榮耀。耶穌是受造界的救贖主。一切曾被罪扭曲的，如今都要蒙祂的恩典觸及；祂是這一切的元首。受造界需要與神和好，或為罪付上刑罰，但耶穌代替受造界付了刑罰。因著祂這樣做，我們得以與神和好，回到主早在伊甸園中創造我們所要擁有的關係。

耶穌藉著在十字架上受死為受造界所做的一切，是我們能與神有真正的和睦與相交的唯一途徑。如今我們在祂面前是聖潔、沒有瑕疵、無可責備的！這就是福音的好消息！保羅因福音的偉大而獻上一生傳揚福音，我們也蒙召這樣做。我們受惠於新約作者及他們對耶穌身分的解釋；但撒該想親自看看祂是誰。他用心靈的眼睛認出耶穌是他的主和救贖主，並選擇信靠祂。我們當中作了同樣選擇的人，必須委身為福音服事，在祂所創造的一切中宣揚耶穌的偉大。

question.en: From this passage, write out how you would describe who Jesus is and what He does.
question.zh-Hant: 根據這段經文，寫下你會如何描述耶穌是誰以及祂做了甚麼。

question.en: What does a life in service to the gospel look like practically for a teenager?
question.zh-Hant: 對青少年來說，在實際生活中為福音服事是甚麼樣子？

prayer.en: Jesus, You have made me holy, blameless, and faultless. You have redeemed Your creation for Your glory. Teach me to live as a servant of the gospel.
prayer.zh-Hant: 耶穌，祢使我成為聖潔、沒有瑕疵、無可責備。祢救贖祢所創造的一切，為了祢的榮耀。求祢教導我作福音的僕人。
